newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: UK backs LDCs on rejecting trade-labour link.
newsitem.headline: UK backs LDCs on rejecting trade-labour link.

text.p: Britain threw its weight on Monday behind developing countries in their rejection of attempts to link trade and labour standards.

Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang told the ministerial meeting of the World Trade Organisation that the International Labour Organisation, not the WTO, was the right forum for promoting workplace standards.
"While Britain is as strongly opposed to child labour and forced labour as anyone else, we see no case for taking trade measures in support of social standards," Lang said.
He said most of European industry shared this view.

"We know it is also the view of most other countries around the world. Let us not divide the WTO on this issue," he told fellow ministers at the opening session of the group's week-long inaugural ministerial meeting.

By contrast, Lang said he favoured a comprehensive work programme in preparation for a new conference of WTO ministers that he said should take place early in 1998 -- the 50th anniversary of the WTO's predecessor, the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade.
Lang said he sympathised with those countries that say they have enough on their plate digesting the results of the Uruguay Round of trade liberalisation measures concluded in 1994.
But he said it was urgent to drive forward the agenda of free trade by focusing on the issues of government procurement, investment and cutting through red tape binding exporters and importers.
The goal, he said, should be to prepare for the launch of a new multilateral trading round before the end of the century that would deliver a big package of liberalisation measures before 2010.
That would set the stage in turn for an even more ambitious goal of global free trade by 2020 -- a regional aim reaffirmed last month by the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
"If the whole of APEC can set itself a target for free trade by 2020, why cannot the WTO do the same? Lang asked.
